notesStmt.note: Whitman's note in blue pencil gives a date of "Dec '88" for the manuscript on the verso, but in a letter to Richard Maurice Bucke, dated November 10, 1888, Whitman writes that he has "finished the little beginning & end Notes I spoke of for the big book and sent to the printer." It therefore seems that this manuscript was written sometime in late October or early November of 1888.
A manuscript draft that is likely related to "Note at End of Complete Poems and Prose," a newly added conclusion that Whitman wrote for that volume, published in 1889.

The verso contains a draft of "Note at Beginning," which also appeared in Complete Poems and Prose. Whitman's note in blue pencil, at the top of the recto, is in reference to that draft.

body.p: . . . The early summer of 1888 bro't me abt the sixth and (as it proves) the most obstinate attack of a paralysis incurred out of from emotional and bodily tensions during the Secession years period of 1863–'65—and prostrating me soon afterward and ever since. Yet then of late (favorably, after two or three weeks at first) this ‸current spell of '88 has left ‸untouch'd my entire mentality and mainly what other power ‸was indispensablyle needed to formulate November Boughs, and get o ‸the work of getting out the present edition; and such have these this has been my occupation and perseverance the past summer
